b2-talalmanyok-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Kempelen After the Turk
b2-talalmanyok-01.scenario: At an inventors' exhibition in Budapest, a visitor named Anna asks what Kempelen Farkas thought of his chess-playing Turk and what he turned to afterwards.
b2-talalmanyok-01.prompt: Tell Anna what Kempelen thought of the Turk and what he built next.
cues: Say what Kempelen thought of the Turk
Say what he turned to and built
b2-talalmanyok-01.target: Kempelen a sakkozó törököt csupán illúziónak tekintette. A tudományosan megoldandó feladatok felé fordult, és megalkotta a beszélőgépet.
b2-talalmanyok-01.english: Kempelen regarded the chess-playing Turk as merely an illusion. He turned to tasks to be solved scientifically and built the speaking machine.
b2-talalmanyok-01.canDo: I can describe Farkas Kempelen's Chess-Playing Turk, his acoustic speaking machine, and his hydraulic engineering works.

b2-talalmanyok-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Light for Rome
b2-talalmanyok-02.scenario: At the Ganz museum in Budapest, a guide named Péter asks what the Ganz engineers patented in 1885 and what they did in Rome in 1892.
b2-talalmanyok-02.prompt: Tell Péter what the Ganz engineers patented and what they lit up in 1892.
cues: Say what they lit up in 1892 and by what means
b2-talalmanyok-02.target: A Ganz-mérnökök 1885-ben szabadalmaztatták a transzformátort. A tivoli vízierőmű révén 1892-ben Róma egy részét kivilágították.
b2-talalmanyok-02.english: The Ganz engineers patented the transformer in 1885. By means of the Tivoli hydroelectric plant, part of Rome was lit up in 1892.
b2-talalmanyok-02.canDo: I can explain Ányos Jedlik's dynamo principle and the 1885 ZBD transformer invented by Károly Zipernowsky, Miksa Déri, and Ottó Bláthy at the Ganz Works.

b2-talalmanyok-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Bíró's Idea
b2-talalmanyok-03.scenario: In a pen shop in Budapest, a customer named Eszter asks where Bíró László got the idea for the ballpoint pen and who helped him.
b2-talalmanyok-03.prompt: Tell Eszter what Bíró noticed in the printing house and who helped him with the paste.
cues: Say what he noticed in the printing house
Say who helped him and what they worked out
b2-talalmanyok-03.target: Bíró László a nyomdában észrevette, hogy a sűrű nyomdafesték gyorsan megszárad. A testvére, Bíró György segítségével kikísérletezte a megfelelő festékpasztát.
b2-talalmanyok-03.english: In the printing house László Bíró noticed that thick printing ink dries quickly. With the help of his brother György Bíró he worked out the right ink paste.
b2-talalmanyok-03.canDo: I can narrate how journalist László Bíró and his chemist brother György invented the modern ballpoint pen (biro) from Budapest to Buenos Aires.

b2-talalmanyok-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Thanks to the Laser
b2-talalmanyok-04.scenario: At a physics club evening in Budapest, a student named Gergő asks what Gábor Dénes invented and why it became an industry.
b2-talalmanyok-04.prompt: Tell Gergő what Gábor Dénes invented and what made it a worldwide industry.
cues: Say what he invented and when
Say what made it an industry and what he received in 1971
b2-talalmanyok-04.target: Gábor Dénes 1947-ben feltalálta a holográfiát. A lézersugárnak köszönhetően a holográfia világméretű iparággá vált, és Gábor Dénes 1971-ben Nobel-díjat kapott.
b2-talalmanyok-04.english: In 1947 Dénes Gábor invented holography. Thanks to the laser beam, holography became a worldwide industry, and in 1971 Dénes Gábor received the Nobel Prize.
b2-talalmanyok-04.canDo: I can explain how Dénes Gábor invented holography in 1947 while trying to improve the electron microscope, earning the 1971 Nobel Prize in Physics.

b2-talalmanyok-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Rubik Built It
b2-talalmanyok-05.scenario: At a design fair in Budapest, a visitor named Kata asks why Rubik Ernő made his cube and how it reached the world.
b2-talalmanyok-05.prompt: Tell Kata what problem Rubik was looking to solve and how the cube reached the world.
cues: Say what problem Rubik wanted to solve
Say how the cube reached the world
b2-talalmanyok-05.target: Rubik Ernő 1974-ben egy szemléltetendő geometriai problémára keresett megoldást. A nemzetközi forgalmazás révén a kocka áttörte a vasfüggönyt.
b2-talalmanyok-05.english: In 1974 Ernő Rubik was looking for a solution to a geometric problem to be demonstrated. Through international distribution the cube broke through the Iron Curtain.
b2-talalmanyok-05.canDo: I can tell the story of how architect Ernő Rubik created the Magic Cube (Bűvös kocka) in 1974 in Budapest to teach three-dimensional geometry.

b2-talalmanyok-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: From Kempelen to Rubik
b2-talalmanyok-consolidation.scenario: At the end of an inventors' exhibition in Budapest, a guest named Réka asks you to name an invention from the exhibition and what became of the Rubik cube.
b2-talalmanyok-consolidation.prompt: Tell Réka what Kempelen built and what the Rubik cube became.
b2-talalmanyok-consolidation.target: Kempelen Farkas beszélőgépet épített. Rubik Ernő kockája a térbeli gondolkodás követendő modelljévé vált.
b2-talalmanyok-consolidation.english: Farkas Kempelen built a speaking machine. Ernő Rubik's cube became a model to be followed of spatial thinking.
b2-talalmanyok-consolidation.canDo: I can explain the scientific and historical significance of Farkas Kempelen, Ányos Jedlik, the Ganz engineers, László Bíró, Dénes Gábor, and Ernő Rubik.
